entities.summary:
The Battles of Bedriacum were two pivotal battles fought in 69 CE, marking a turning point in the Year of the Four Emperors. 

The first battle, fought in April 69, saw the forces of Vitellius, a Roman general, clash with those of Otho, a Roman senator. 

The second battle, fought in October 69, saw the forces of Vitellius, now Emperor, defeat those of Vespasian, a Roman general, in a decisive victory. 

The outcome of these battles led to the downfall of Otho and the rise of Vitellius, but he was soon overthrown by Vespasian, who went on to found the Flavian dynasty, a period of relative peace and prosperity in Rome. 

The Battles of Bedriacum, fought in the heart of Italy, were a crucial moment in the annals of Roman history, shaping the course of imperial power and paving the way for the rise of a new dynasty. 

'One of the most crucial, and least known, battles in Roman history.' - Edward Gibbon, The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire.
